title: The Discipline of Computing
description: Orientation to computing as a field of study for students considering a Computer Science major, a Cyber Security major, or a Computer Science minor.
learning_objectives: Describe career paths and subfields within computing
Evaluate fit for a computing major or minor
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 121-001, Fall 2023

title: Computer Science I
description: First course in the CS-major programming sequence: variables, control flow, functions, and structured problem solving.
learning_objectives: Write and debug structured programs
Apply control structures and functions to solve problems
source: UA 2021-24 Computer Science Curriculum flowchart (no syllabus provided for this course number in this project's reference set)

title: CS II for Majors
description: Second programming course for CS majors: object-oriented practices, fundamental data structures, computability, problem complexity, and efficient searching and sorting.
learning_objectives: Apply object-oriented programming practices
Analyze algorithm complexity for searching and sorting
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 101-002, Spring 2024

title: Software Design and Engineering
description: Software engineering practice across the program life cycle: systems analysis, software modeling, design theory and practice, testing methodology, team organization, and verification.
learning_objectives: Apply software design and modeling techniques
Practice team-based development and testing methodology
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 200-001, Fall 2024

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Data structures including balanced search trees, heaps, hash tables, and graphs, plus algorithm design techniques such as divide-and-conquer, greedy methods, and dynamic programming.
learning_objectives: Select and implement appropriate data structures
Apply core algorithm design techniques and analyze their complexity
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 201-001, Spring 2025

title: Web Foundations
description: Fundamentals of the internet and web page design and development, including HTML, hyperlinks, tables, basic CSS styling, frames, and forms.
learning_objectives: Build web pages using HTML and CSS
Apply basic client-side web development techniques
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 202-910, Fall 2023

title: Introduction to Python Programming
description: Introduction to programming and problem solving using Python.
learning_objectives: Write Python programs to solve structured problems
Apply general problem-solving strategies in a high-level language
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 223-910, Fall 2024

title: Digital Logic
description: Number systems, Boolean algebra, logic functions and gates, design of combinational logic systems, flip-flops, and design of synchronous sequential systems, with laboratory experiments.
learning_objectives: Design combinational and sequential logic circuits
Apply Boolean algebra to digital circuit design
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: ECE 380-001, Fall 2024

title: Microcomputers
description: Microprocessors, microcontrollers, assembly-language programming, interrupts, polling, and hardware interfaces, with laboratory experiments.
learning_objectives: Write assembly-language programs for a microcontroller
Interface software with hardware peripherals via interrupts and polling
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: ECE 383-001, Fall 2025

title: Operating Systems
description: Core operating-system concepts, including process management, memory management, concurrency, and file systems.
learning_objectives: Explain process and memory management strategies
Reason about concurrency and synchronization in an OS
source: UA 2021-24 Computer Science Curriculum flowchart (no syllabus provided for this course number in this project's reference set)

title: Database Management Systems
description: Constituent parts of database management: design, creation, and manipulation of databases, including conceptual and relational data models, SQL, normalization, and security.
learning_objectives: Design a normalized relational schema
Write SQL for common data manipulation and query tasks
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 301-002, Fall 2025

title: Programming Languages
description: Formal study of programming language specification, analysis, implementation, and run-time support structures, including language constructs and non-procedural programming paradigms.
learning_objectives: Compare programming paradigms and language design choices
Analyze run-time support structures for a language implementation
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 403-001, Fall 2026

title: Software Design & Development
description: Modern software engineering practice for reliable, maintainable systems: requirements analysis, software architecture and design patterns, agile methodology, version control workflows, automated testing, and CI/CD. Teams design, implement, test, and deploy a medium-scale software project.
learning_objectives: Apply agile methodology and design patterns to a team software project
Build and operate a CI/CD workflow for a deployed application
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 415-001, Fall 2026

title: Intro to Autonomous Robotics
description: Implementation of robot control software, including motion, kinematics, simulation testing, sensor incorporation, and unmodeled factors.
learning_objectives: Implement basic robot motion and kinematics control
Incorporate sensor data into robot control software
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 460-001, Fall 2026

title: Brain Computer Interface
description: New forms of human-computer interaction based on passive measurement of neurophysiological states, including cognitive workload and affective engagement.
learning_objectives: Explain approaches to passive neurophysiological measurement
Connect physiological signal data to human-computer interaction design
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 461-001, Spring 2026

title: Computer Algorithms
description: Construction of efficient algorithms for computer implementation.
learning_objectives: Design and analyze efficient algorithms
Select an algorithmic strategy appropriate to a problem's constraints
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 470-001, Spring 2026

title: Theory of Computing
description: Theoretical foundations of computing, offered as an alternative to CS 470 in the curriculum's Theory requirement.
learning_objectives: Reason about computability and formal models of computation
Apply theoretical models to analyze algorithm limits
source: UA 2021-24 Computer Science Curriculum flowchart, listed as an alternative to CS 470 (no syllabus provided for this course number in this project's reference set)

title: High Performance Computing
description: Fundamental concepts of high performance computing, including optimizing sequential programs for modern memory hierarchies, parallel algorithm design, developing parallel programs with MPI, and analyzing parallel program performance.
learning_objectives: Design a parallel algorithm for a computational problem
Analyze the performance of a parallel program
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 481-001, Spring 2026

title: Capstone Computing
description: Culminating capstone project course integrating skills and abilities from across the curriculum into a comprehensive design and development experience for computer science majors.
learning_objectives: Integrate prior coursework into a comprehensive software project
Communicate a completed project's design and development process in writing
source: UA Computer Science syllabus: CS 495-001, Fall 2026
